hints: Focus on what dehydration actually does, it removes water to create a C=C double bond between two carbons.
Check each alcohol for how many carbons it has, methanol with only one carbon has nowhere to form a C=C bond.
Test the other two alcohols for a hydrogen on the carbon next to the C-OH group, if they have it they can lose water to give an alkene.
walkthrough:
**Recall the dehydration rule**

Think of dehydration as pulling $\text{H}$ and $\text{OH}$ from neighbouring carbons to make a double bond.

General idea:
$$\text{alcohol} \rightarrow \text{alkene} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Test alcohol 1, methanol**

Methanol is $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$ with only one carbon, so there is no second carbon to form $\text{C=C}$ with.

It cannot give an alkene, it can only give other products like an ether under different conditions.

**Test alcohols 2 and 3**

Alcohol 2 is $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{COH}$, a tertiary alcohol, and alcohol 3 is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$, a secondary alcohol.

Both have at least two carbons and hydrogens on adjacent carbons:
$$ (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{COH} \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} $$
$$ \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} $$

**Conclude which cannot react**

Only alcohol 1 lacks the structure needed for alkene formation, while 2 and 3 dehydrate easily.

So the answer is 1 only.

options.A: This option suggests 1, 2 and 3 all cannot form alkenes. That is wrong because 2 and 3 both dehydrate readily to give 2-methylpropene and propene.
options.B: This option suggests 1 and 2 cannot form alkenes. Alcohol 1 is correct, but alcohol 2 is a tertiary alcohol that dehydrates very easily, so this combination is wrong.
options.C: This option suggests 2 and 3 cannot form alkenes. This is the opposite of the truth, as both 2 and 3 have adjacent C-H bonds and form alkenes quickly with acid and heat.
options.D: This option states only 1 cannot form an alkene. Methanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$, has only one carbon so a C=C bond is impossible, while 2 and 3 can both eliminate water to form alkenes.
